evidence.title: Add the Plausible tracking script
evidence.text:
If you write your site's pages by hand as HTML files, each page has its own `<head>` section, so there's no single header to add the snippet to. Paste the snippet into the `<head>` of every page you want to count, for example right below the `<title>` line:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <title>My site</title>
    <!-- Paste your Plausible snippet here -->
  </head>
  <body>
    ...
  </body>
</html>
```

Then upload the files to your web host as usual. Pages without the snippet aren't counted, so add it to every new page you create too. Your site doesn't need any JavaScript of its own: the snippet is all Plausible needs.

If you use a static site generator such as Hugo, Jekyll or Eleventy, add the snippet once to the layout or template that all your pages share instead.

question: i manage like 40 client sites that all need the same Signup goal. is there a faster way than clicking through each one?
reference_answer: Yes, run a short script that calls PUT /api/v1/sites/goals for each domain with goal_type "event" and event_name "Signup". The endpoint finds or creates the goal, so running it again leaves sites that already have it unchanged. You can get the list of domains from GET /api/v1/sites.
key_facts: Endpoint finds or creates, so it is idempotent
answer:
If you run many sites that track the same events, you can add them to every site in one go with a short script instead of one site at a time [1]. Put your domains in a list, then call PUT /api/v1/sites/goals and PUT /api/v1/sites/custom-props for each one [1]:

```bash title="Add a goal and a custom property to several sites"
for site in site1.com site2.com site3.com; do
  curl -X PUT https://plausible.io/api/v1/sites/goals \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "{\"site_id\": \"$site\", \"goal_type\": \"event\", \"event_name\": \"Signup\"}"

  curl -X PUT https://plausible.io/api/v1/sites/custom-props \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
    -F "site_id=$site" \
    -F "property=plan"
  echo
done
```

evidence.title: Site provisioning API reference
evidence.text:
Goals and custom properties are set up per site. If you run many sites that track the same events, such as a network of client sites or one site per customer, you can add them to every site in one go with a short script instead of one site at a time.

Put your domains in a list, then call PUT /api/v1/sites/goals and PUT /api/v1/sites/custom-props for each one:

```bash title="Add a goal and a custom property to several sites"
for site in site1.com site2.com site3.com; do
  curl -X PUT https://plausible.io/api/v1/sites/goals \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "{\"site_id\": \"$site\", \"goal_type\": \"event\", \"event_name\": \"Signup\"}"

  curl -X PUT https://plausible.io/api/v1/sites/custom-props \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
    -F "site_id=$site" \
    -F "property=plan"
  echo
done
```

To get the domains of your team's sites, call GET /api/v1/sites. With a Sites API key, it lists only the sites of the team the key belongs to, which are the ones the key can change. Both endpoints find or create, so running the script again leaves sites that already have the goal or property as they are. Run the same calls right after creating a new site to give it the setup your other sites have.

question: im on a vpn and my ip keeps changing so blocking my IP in settings doesnt really work. how do i stop counting my own visits?
reference_answer: If your IP changes often or you use a VPN, set the exclusion flag yourself in your browser. Open the Console tab in the developer tools on your site and run localStorage.plausible_ignore=true, and repeat for every domain, subdomain and browser you want to exclude.
key_facts: Use a localStorage flag instead of an IP block
Run localStorage.plausible_ignore=true in the browser console
Repeat for each domain, subdomain and browser
answer:
You can set a special `localStorage` flag in your browser so you don't need to frequently block new IP addresses [1]. Open the Console tab in your browser's developer tools on your site, then paste this command and hit enter:

Do this for every domain, subdomain and browser you want to exclude [2].

citations.quote: You can then set a special `localStorage` flag in your browser so you don't need to frequently block new IP addresses.

Open the **Console** tab in your browser's developer tools on your site, then paste this command and hit enter:

```html
localStorage.plausible_ignore=true
```
Do this for every domain, subdomain and browser you want to exclude.

evidence.title: Let visitors opt out of being counted
evidence.text:
To keep your own visits or your team's out of your stats, block your IP addresses in your site settings. That works across all your browsers and devices at once.

If your IP address changes often or you use a VPN, you can set the same flag yourself instead. Open the **Console** tab in your browser's developer tools on your site, then paste this command and hit enter:

```html
localStorage.plausible_ignore=true
```

Do this for every domain, subdomain and browser you want to exclude. To be counted again, run:

```html
delete localStorage.plausible_ignore
```

You can also use the opt-out page above instead of the console.

evidence.text:
Credit/debit card, PayPal, Apple Pay and Google Pay. All payment processing is handled by Paddle. Larger annual plans can also be paid by invoice and bank transfer on request. We're not able to accept cryptocurrency.

Paddle automatically emails you an invoice after every payment. Our purchasing and vendor information page covers company details and purchasing documents.
